title: Exact Haar Statistics of Planar $k$-Purity in Multipartite Quantum Systems
abstract: Planar $k$-uniform states have maximally mixed reductions on every $k$-site interval of a ring. We introduce planar $k$-purity---the mean purity of those intervals---as a faithful cost function for this simultaneous constraint. For a Haar-random pure state of $n$ parties with local dimension $p$, the joint purity of two intervals depends only on their overlap. An exhaustive four-replica calculation therefore yields the complete cyclic covariance kernel and a closed variance for every $1\le k\le\lfloor n/2\rfloor$. In the balanced qubit case, $k=\lfloor n/2\rfloor$ and $N=2^n$, the variance is asymptotic to $20/(3nN^2)$ for even $n$ and $6/(nN^2)$ for odd $n$. A site-factorized permutation representation gives all raw moments and permits exact finite-sum evaluation of the skewness. Fixed-seed simulations validate nonbalanced qubit and qutrit cases, while balanced-qubit simulations through $n=10$ validate the parity formulas and finite-size skewness. Balanced planar and absolute balanced purity have the same Haar mean but different fluctuations; the planar variance is approximately $2.83$ times larger at $n=10$. Thus subsystem incidence, although invisible to every one-cut marginal distribution, controls the collective fluctuations of geometrically related cuts. Together with universal attainability and a linear number of interval constraints at balance, this provides a geometry-aware benchmark for multipartite entanglement beyond AME existence regimes.
summary: This paper calculates the exact statistical moments, including the variance, for a measure called planar $k$-purity in multipartite quantum systems. By analyzing how purity depends on the overlap of geometrically related subsystems, it reveals that local correlations (subsystem incidence) control collective fluctuations even when single-cut marginals appear featureless. This offers a powerful, geometry-aware tool for characterizing multipartite entanglement.
main_problem: The paper aims to quantify multipartite entanglement in pure quantum states by analyzing the statistical properties of planar $k$-purity.
main_result: It derives exact closed-form expressions for the mean, covariance kernel, and variance of planar $k$-purity for Haar-random states, showing that planar fluctuations are distinct from those governed by single-cut marginals.
method: The analysis uses advanced theoretical techniques involving replica calculations, site-factorized permutation representations, and the application of generalized trace formulas on replicated quantum states.
model_or_system: The system is a multipartite quantum state of $n$ parties with local dimension $p$, specifically focusing on Haar-random pure states distributed on a ring geometry.
key_observables: Planar $k$-purity ($\pi^{(k)}_P$), joint purity of two intervals, and the variance of these purity measures.
important_parameters: The number of parties ($n$), the local dimension ($p$), and the interval size ($k$).
main_assumptions: The calculations assume the state is Haar-random and focus on the planar constraint, which is a specific geometric restriction on entanglement.
figures_summary: Figure 1 illustrates the geometry for planar $k$-purity, showing an interval and its translation with a defined overlap.
paper_structure: The paper develops the theory by first defining planar $k$-purity as a cost function, then deriving the joint purity moments using replica methods, and finally presenting closed-form expressions and asymptotic limits for the variance.
why_interesting: The work provides a rigorous, geometry-aware benchmark for entanglement beyond simple marginal constraints, which is crucial for understanding how local correlations dictate global quantum properties in many-body systems.
